findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews overdue notice counts on the first of every month. Historical figures are archived for five years before being summarized and retired."
findings.fix: Add specific data showing current annual overdue fine revenue, historical trends in fine collection rates or return patterns, and baseline circulation statistics for comparison context.
findings.violation: This section describes data collection procedures but provides no actual circulation metrics, fine revenue figures, or historical trends needed to establish the current baseline before recommending a major policy change.

findings.evidence: "The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot" (pilot duration: 18 months total)
findings.fix: Provide survey data from month 18 when the pilot concluded, or explain why the interim 12-month measurement, rather than the final result, is the appropriate basis for this recommendation.
findings.violation: The post-intervention survey was conducted at 12 months, not at the end of the 18-month pilot period, leaving a 6-month gap where patron sentiment may have continued to shift.

findings.evidence: "This is simply how patron behavior works, and no library that has tried it has ever found otherwise."
findings.fix: Either provide citations to peer-reviewed studies on fine elimination outcomes in other library systems, or add a comparison table demonstrating that the 5 pilot branches are representative of the other 5 branches in size, location type, patron demographics, and usage patterns.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section
findings.violation: This section does not actually justify why results from 5 specific branches apply to all 10 branches, and makes an unsupported universal claim about library behavior without evidence or citations.

findings.evidence: "A skeptic on the board points to overdue fines as a source of materials-replacement funding, and argues that eliminating them systemwide will leave a shortfall the consortium has not planned for. The branch renovation project remains on schedule for completion next spring."
findings.fix: Provide analysis showing (1) current annual revenue from overdue fines, (2) projected annual revenue from replacement-cost billing on items unreturned past 60 days, and (3) how any remaining shortfall will be covered.
findings.violation: The section acknowledges a legitimate funding shortfall concern but does not address it; the closing statement about the renovation project is disconnected and provides no financial solution.

findings.evidence: "items still unreturned past that window remain subject to the existing replacement-cost billing process, matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established"
findings.fix: Add analysis of the pilot's return-timing distribution (what percentage returned by day 30, 45, 60, and beyond) and project the expected annual revenue from replacement-cost billing to demonstrate financial feasibility.
findings.violation: The document provides no data on what percentage or number of items exceed the 60-day return threshold or what revenue the replacement-cost billing would generate, making it impossible to assess whether this adequately compensates for lost fine revenue.
